People at Increased Risk for Food Poisoning Jan. 31, 2025 Key points Certain groups of people are at higher risk for severe illness from foodborne illness. Higher risk groups include people who are 65 and older, children under 5, people with weakened immune systems, and pregnant women. People at increased risk Anyone can get food poisoning, but certain groups of people are more likely to get very sick from food poisoning. For these people, their body may not be able to fight germs and sickness as effectively. It's especially important to take steps to prevent food poisoning if you or someone you care for belong to one of the groups below. People 65 and older People aged 65 and older are at increased risk for food poisoning. As people age, their immune systems and organs don't recognize and get rid of harmful germs as well as they once did. This increases the chance they'll get sick from food poisoning. Nearly half of people aged 65 and older who have a lab-confirmed foodborne illness from Salmonella , Campylobacter , Listeria or E. coli are hospitalized. High-risk animals Turtles can carry germs that can make some people very sick. The depth and extent of this “permafrost” varies by location, depending on average air temperatures, soil types, topography, and surface vegetation. Frozen ground is stable, providing a solid foundation for roads and buildings. Permafrost is also impermeable, so water pools on the surface instead of seeping through the soil, and creates a landscape dotted with many small lakes. The shorter and warmer winters are affecting permafrost. – Dave Swanson, Fairbanks Rising temperatures are melting this frozen ground and forever altering the landscape. Without this solid foundation, roads and buildings sink into the softer, non-frozen ground. Sinkholes and slumpages form when their frozen supportive underground layers thaw. pages.text: Personal Assistance Services | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Personal Assistance Services More in This Section Close Accessible Technology Communications Access Health Care Housing Personal Assistance Services Transportation Universal Design For many individuals with disabilities, personal assistance services (PAS) help make employment possible. Some people use PAS to carry out activities of daily living. Depending on the individual, such activities might include getting up and ready for work, bathing, dressing, cooking, cleaning, or running errands. Some people also use PAS in the workplace. Examples of workplace PAS vary, but may involve activities such as retrieving materials out of reach or providing travel assistance for an employee with a mobility impairment; helping an employee with a cognitive disability in decision-making; reading printed materials to an employee who is visually impaired; or ensuring a sign language interpreter is present during meetings for an employee who is deaf. Whether at home or work, PAS can be essential to employment success. Recognizing this, ODEP works to expand and raise awareness of employment-related PAS options. Meeting the needs of people on and off the job raises important policy issues for federal and state governments, service providers, and employers, as well as people with disabilities themselves. ODEP recognizes PAS is a critical issue — not only for those seeking employment, but also for those already employed. Foley – named after the pioneerng Warner Brothers sound engineer Jack Foley – is the art of creating sounds in sync with the picture, from footsteps and rustling clothes to the movements of creatures. He won two Emmy awards, for Band of Brothers, in 2002, and Generation Kill, in 2009. History In 2010, a paper map by 3dShapes was digitized and imported, to map landuse in Nederland. The import project was well conducted and properly documented in the OSM-wiki. This was a major step in filling in the space on OSM. Some problems remained after import, to be dealt with later. For instance, where trees had been planted in multiple rows, it was imported as an orchard. As a result, our motorways were suddenly lined with orchards, on OSM-based maps. This has been fixed by organized mappings. Another example: the paper map had a tile grid of thin black lines. These lines were seen as cut lines, resulting in unnecessary and awkward splits of the imported areas. The import procedure did detect this problem, but couldn’t automate a fix, so this was left to the future mappers. It took 15 years before a crazy mapper got rid of this in a solo project lasting 2 months. Guess who? pages.text: Peter Storey: Former Arsenal and England midfielder dies aged 81 - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Peter Storey won 19 caps for England Published 17 November 2026 Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81. Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals. He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee. "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement. "All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. "We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund." Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield. He is currently eighth on Arsenal 's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions. Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72. Petroglyphs , images carved into rock, and pictographs , images painted onto rock surfaces, take both abstract forms, such as spirals and lines, and recognizable animal or human shapes. The symbols are both art and a means of communication. In some places petroglyphs and pictographs are so prolific that a national monument was set aside to preserve them. Many are just part of the landscape already protected. Discover stories of how they were found. Find out how we study what they mean. Learn where you can see rock art in the national parks. Phil Kangas Deputy Director, Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) Phil Kangas is the Deputy Director of the Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF), focusing on the Office's operations and mission delivery. He previously served as the Acting Deputy Director and Division Director for Outreach and Business Development (OBD), where he led efforts to source quality project applications. Prior to joining DOE, Mr. Kangas spent 25 years in the private sector as a management consultant, including a 20+ year career at Grant Thornton LLP, where he led the firm’s National Energy Advisory practice for clients in the natural resources, mining, and renewables sectors. He also led the federal sciences portfolio for work delivered at DOE, Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), National Science Foundation (NSF), and National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). Mr. Kangas earned a Bachelor of Arts in History and Political Science from John Carroll University and a Master of Public Administration from Syracuse University’s Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs.

For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet. It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert. Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side programming language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks. Governments and cyber-security agencies rushed to contain the fallout , urging website owners to check if their sites were affected and, if so, install updates to patch the issue or consider going offline. There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far. But in the days since the issues came to light, disruption to sites and services has continued to ripple around the world. What is PHP? Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily. It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server. Public Library Archives Birmingham Civil Rights National Monument was established in 2017, and encompasses roughly four city blocks in downtown Birmingham, Alabama. The National Monument includes the A.G. Gaston Motel, which served as the headquarters for the Birmingham campaign. From April through May of 1963, leaders of the civil rights movement, including Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., took up residence at the motel. Here they strategized and made critical decisions about the non-violent campaign that targeted Birmingham’s segregation laws and practices. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Canyons of the Ancients National Monument | Colorado View Map In Full Screen Canyons of the Ancients National Monument, located in the Four Corners region of southwestern Colorado, protects a stunning cultural landscape with the highest known density of archaeological sites in the United States. Encompassing 176,000 acres of public lands, the Monument features more than 8,300 documented sites—including villages, kivas, field houses, cliff dwellings, petroglyphs, and ancient roadways—with estimates suggesting over 30,000 yet to be recorded. These sites offer a window into over 12,000 years of human history, primarily shaped by Ancestral Puebloan cultures and their descendants. The area continues to be a living landscape used today for traditional purposes, recreation, hunting, livestock grazing, and energy development. It also encompasses Cross Canyon , Sego Lily, and Cahone Canyon Wilderness Study Areas. While exploring the Monument’s canyons, mesas, and desert terrain, visitors are reminded to Visit with Respect and Leave No Trace to protect the resources that define this unique place.
